class electrip.widgets.ControlPointGraph(x_legend_text, y_legend_text, x_res_list, y_res_list)[source]¶

Bases: gi.repository.Gtk.DrawingArea

Graph-widget allowing to edit a LinearSegmentFunction visually in a cartesian coordinate system. x_legend_text and y_legend_text specify the labels for the x- and y-axis. x_res_list and y_res_list are lists containing acceptable resolutions for the x- and y-axis.

Behaviour:

  • Left-click: Creates a new control-point
  • Left-click + drag: Drags an existing control-point
  • Right-click: Removes an existing control-point

class electrip.widgets.EntryTable(use_tooltips, use_bold_labels, orientation=<enum GTK_ORIENTATION_VERTICAL of type GtkOrientation>, end=None)[source]¶

Bases: gi.repository.Gtk.Grid

Provides a UI to set attributes on configuration objects. Allows you to stop caring about signal-handling and layout.

If use_tooltips is True, the descriptions are provided as tooltips. Otherwise the description will appear behind the ui-elements. If use_bold_labels is True, the labels for the object-attributes appear in bold font.

New input-elements can be added using the ‘add_(some_element)’-methods, where the first two arguments specify the label and the description-text for the respective attribute.

Have a look at the following example:

# NOTE: we assume a Loco-instance called 'loco'
# has already been created

# choose layout-options on creation
table = EntryTable(True, False)

# add a combo-box which operates on loco.protocol
table.add_combo_entry("Protokoll",
                      "Das Digitalprotokoll, welches"
                      "vom Decoder verwendet wird.",
                      "protocol",
                      GObject.TYPE_STRING,
                      (("M 1", "Märklin Motorola Version 1"),
                       ("M 2", "Märklin Motorola Version 2"),
                       ("N 1", "DCC kurzes Adressformat"),
                       ("N 2", "DCC langes Adressformat")))

# you can add more ui-elements for different attributes 
table.add_...

# load the protocol value from loco
# and the others you have specified
table.load(loco)

# now, if the user selects "Märklin Motorola Version 1",
# "M 1" will be stored in loco.protocol
add_action_button(label, description, button_label, callback)[source]¶

Adds a Gtk.Button with button_label which calls callback when clicked.

add_bool_entry(label, description, config_attribute)[source]¶

Adds a Gtk.CheckButton for boolean values.

add_combo_entry(label, description, config_attribute, content_type, mapping)[source]¶

Adds a EasyComboBox.

content_type specifies the type of the values to be stored in the combobox (e.g. GObject.TYPE_STRING, ...). mapping is a list of 2-tuples, which maps values stored in the model to the displayed values. Example: see EntryTable.

add_float_entry(label, description, config_attribute, min_value=0.0, max_value=9999.0, step=0.1)[source]¶

Adds a Gtk.SpinButton for floats.

min_value and max_value specify the value range for the float. step specifies the precision of the number as step between two possible values.

add_image_file_entry(label, description, config_attribute)[source]¶

Adds an EasyFileButton for image-file selection.

add_int_entry(label, description, config_attribute, min_value=0, max_value=9999, step=1)[source]¶

Adds a Gtk.SpinButton.

min_value and max_value specify the value range for the integer. step specifies the step between two possible values. step must not be an integer, but the values will be converted to integers before being stored.

Adds a Label with a text according to markup.

add_string_entry(label, description, config_attribute)[source]¶

load(config_object)[source]¶

Loads the values for the user interface elements from config_object.

save_changes(widget, config_attrib)[source]¶

Transports changes from the user-interface to the EntryTable.config_object which was set using EntryTable.load(). This method is called automatically whenever the user changes an element which was added using one of the ‘add_(some_element)’-methods.

class electrip.widgets.TreeView(name)[source]¶

Bases: gi.overrides.Gtk.TreeView

A simplified TreeView, allowing to easily add columns and transport changes back to a datamodel.

name specifies the name of the TreeView, used for the ‘unsaved-changes’-messages.

Example::
class CustomTreeView(TreeView):
def __init__(self):

widgets.TreeView.__init__(self, “CustomTreeView”) self.add_text_colum(“Eine Text-Spalte”,

“Name der Spalte”, GObject.TYPE_STRING)
self.add_non_editable_text_colum(“Geräuschdatei”,
“Datei für die Wiedergabe ” “(‘.wav’ oder ‘.ogg’)”, GObject.TYPE_STRING)

self.add_more_stuff ... self.update_model()

self.connect(“row-activated”, self.choose_sound)

add_column(column_name, column_tooltip, cell_renderer, content_type)[source]¶

Adds a new column using cell_renderer.

add_combo_colum(column_name, column_tooltip, content_type, values)[source]¶

Adds a column with Gtk.ComboBox-widgets.

For column_name and column_tooltip see add_text_column(). content_type defines the type of the values to be stored in the combobox (e.g. str, float ...). values is a list of the values the user can choose from.

add_non_editable_text_colum(column_name, column_tooltip, content_type)[source]¶

Adds a column with non-editable text. For arguments, see add_text_column().

add_text_colum(column_name, column_tooltip, content_type)[source]¶

Adds a column with editable text. The column_name is displayed above the column and the column_tooltip appears when the mouse hovers over the colums header.

new_value(cellrenderer, path, new_value)[source]¶
save_changes(path, column_nr, new_value)[source]¶

This method is called whenever a value of a cell in the TreeView has changed. Child classes should make use of this.

path: a Gtk.TreePath to the respective cell. column_nr: number of the column where the change occured new_value: the new value of the cell

update_model()[source]¶

Overwrites the old liststore (if there is any) with the current column-setup. Must be called after all columns have been added.
